title: The Globe Of The Earth Its Journey And The Proofs Of Mercy On The Page Of Spring

questions.question: What invitation does the earth give the traveler at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It calls him away from wandering through the sky and tells him to examine the earth’s works and learn from them.

questions.question: How is the earth’s movement pictured in a vivid comparison?
questions.answer: It is compared to a whirling dervish turning with two motions.

questions.question: What results from the earth’s motion according to the passage?
questions.answer: It brings about the cycle of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the earth described as a great ship?
questions.answer: Because it carries huge amounts of supplies and necessities for living creatures while traveling in space in a balanced way.

questions.question: What does the traveler notice when he studies the earth like a book?
questions.answer: He sees that its pages and sections point again and again to its Lord.

questions.question: Which part of the earth’s “book” does he focus on especially?
questions.answer: He focuses on the springtime page about the coming forth and spreading of living things.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the origin of many life-forms in spring?
questions.answer: Their many shapes come out from simple matter with great precision.

questions.question: What happens to some seeds in a remarkable way?
questions.answer: Some are given means to travel through the air so they can spread to other places.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the care given to living things after they appear?
questions.answer: They are distributed, fed, and raised with great care and mercy.

questions.question: What contrast is used to show divine power in providing food?
questions.answer: Delicious foods are produced from plain earth and from similar-looking roots, seeds, and drops of fluid.

questions.question: What image is used for how spring provision reaches living beings?
questions.answer: It is like supplies being loaded from an unseen storehouse onto a railcar and then sent out in perfect order.

questions.question: Why is feeding babies given special attention in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows a very tender form of care, wisdom, and mercy through the nourishment prepared for them through their mothers.

questions.question: What larger belief does the revival of the earth in spring support?
questions.answer: It supports belief that the One who revives dead land can also raise the dead.

questions.question: In what sense is spring called a sign of the Supreme Gathering?
questions.answer: It shows countless examples of life returning after death, which points to resurrection.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from the earth’s pages?
questions.answer: He understands that all of them declare the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Why does the earth tell the traveler to look at its functions and pages?
questions.answer: It wants to show him the signs that answer what he has been seeking.

questions.question: What do the earth’s two movements suggest about order in the universe?
questions.answer: They show that its motion is controlled in a way that produces regular patterns in time.

questions.question: What does the phrase about food and equipment for living beings suggest about the earth?
questions.answer: It suggests the earth is prepared as a place fully supplied for the needs of creation.

questions.question: Why does the traveler not try to read every page of the earth?
questions.answer: Because its signs are too many, so he chooses one page to study closely.

questions.question: What does the spring page mainly reveal?
questions.answer: It reveals the creation, spreading, and care of living beings.

questions.question: How does the emergence of many species from simple material strengthen the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that complex and distinct life cannot be explained by matter alone but points to wise design.

questions.question: What can be inferred from seeds being spread in effective ways?
questions.answer: Their movement serves a purpose and is managed with knowledge and planning.

questions.question: How does the passage show both power and mercy in food production?
questions.answer: It describes abundant nourishment being brought out from basic materials in a gentle and beneficial way.

questions.question: What does the unseen treasury image teach about provision?
questions.answer: It teaches that the source of sustenance is beyond what people can fully see and comes by divine generosity.

questions.question: Why is a mother’s milk presented as a strong proof of compassion?
questions.answer: Because it is specially prepared for a helpless infant at exactly the right time and in the right form.

questions.question: How does the Qur’anic verse about reviving the earth fit the spring scene?
questions.answer: It matches what the traveler sees in spring, where dead land becomes living again.

questions.question: What link does the passage make between revival in nature and life after death?
questions.answer: The yearly return of life in spring is presented as evidence that resurrection is possible.

questions.question: What does it mean that the earth proclaims faith “according to the size” of its pages?
questions.answer: It means every part of the earth gives witness in a way suited to its own scale and content.

questions.question: State the main message of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The earth, especially in spring, shows through its order, care, and life-giving power that Allah alone is worthy of worship.

questions.question: What change of focus happens at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: The traveler turns from the heavens to the earth to continue his search for signs.

questions.question: How is the earth’s movement both beautiful and meaningful in the description?
questions.answer: It is presented as graceful like a turning dancer and useful because it marks time through recurring cycles.

questions.question: What does the earth’s balance in space suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests control, stability, and deliberate arrangement rather than randomness.

questions.question: Why is the earth compared to a vessel carrying supplies?
questions.answer: Because it supports and transports everything needed for the lives of many creatures.

questions.question: What literary image is used for studying the earth?
questions.answer: The earth is presented as a book with pages and chapters to be read.

questions.question: What does each page of the earth “say,” according to the traveler?
questions.answer: Each one points to the Lordship and sustaining power of Allah.

questions.question: What season receives special attention, and why?
questions.answer: Spring does, because it displays the return and spread of life in a very clear way.

questions.question: How are the many species in spring described in relation to precision?
questions.answer: Their forms appear with exactness even though they arise from simple substances.

questions.question: What is remarkable about the food described in the passage?
questions.answer: Many kinds of appealing nourishment come from sources that seem plain and nearly alike.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the distribution of provision to living beings?
questions.answer: It portrays it as organized, abundant, and sent out from a hidden source.

questions.question: What example especially highlights care for the weak?
questions.answer: The nourishment prepared for babies through their mothers shows special care for those who cannot provide for themselves.

questions.question: Why would this example speak strongly to a thoughtful reader?
questions.answer: Because it shows mercy joined with exact wisdom in meeting a need before the child can even ask.

questions.question: What does the revival of the earth after its dead period demonstrate besides seasonal change?
questions.answer: It demonstrates a sign of divine mercy and a proof of the power to resurrect.

questions.question: How does the passage use spring as an argument for the afterlife?
questions.answer: It treats the yearly restoration of life as a visible model of how the dead can be brought back.

questions.question: What final testimony does the traveler hear from the earth?
questions.answer: He understands that all of its pages witness to the truth that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What is the earth asking the traveler to do instead of roaming through the sky?
questions.answer: It is asking him to study the earth itself and learn from its signs.

questions.question: What do the earth’s two motions accomplish in the passage?
questions.answer: They organize the passing of time through day, year, and season.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the earth is suitable for life?
questions.answer: It describes the earth as carrying provisions and tools needed by countless living things.

questions.question: Why is “utmost equilibrium” important in the description of the earth?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that the earth moves in a steady, controlled way while holding life.

questions.question: What does the traveler learn from even one page of the earth?
questions.answer: He learns that it contains many signs pointing to the One who sustains it.

questions.question: What does spring reveal about the source of living forms?
questions.answer: It reveals that many distinct forms are brought out from simple material by precise power.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning seeds that are enabled to travel?
questions.answer: It shows that spreading life across the earth happens through planned and effective means.

questions.question: How is nourishment described in relation to mercy?
questions.answer: Food is presented as being provided gently, generously, and with compassion.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention dry soil, roots, seeds, and drops of liquid?
questions.answer: To show that rich and varied life-supporting foods come from basic and seemingly ordinary materials.

questions.question: What does the comparison to a loaded railcar suggest about springtime provision?
questions.answer: It suggests careful delivery, large-scale preparation, and order in supplying living beings.

questions.question: How does the example of milk for infants deepen the message of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a close, human example of loving care that people can easily recognize.

questions.question: What qualities are shown in that example besides mercy?
questions.answer: It also shows wisdom, generosity, and thoughtful planning.

questions.question: How does the cited verse about reviving the earth support the traveler’s reflection?
questions.answer: It gives revealed confirmation that bringing life back to dead land is a sign of greater divine power.

questions.question: What is meant by calling spring a visible proof of resurrection?
questions.answer: Spring lets people watch a kind of small-scale return to life that points to the final rising of the dead.

questions.question: What overall confession of faith does the earth lead the traveler to understand?
questions.answer: It leads him to recognize the oneness of Allah through the signs spread across the earth.

questions.question: In this passage, what role does the earth take in relation to the traveler?
questions.answer: It acts like a guide that teaches him through its condition and activities.

questions.question: How does the description of the earth’s motion combine movement and order?
questions.answer: Although it is constantly turning, it does so in a way that produces stable patterns for life.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the earth being full of supplies for living creatures?
questions.answer: Life on earth is not left unsupported but is provided for intentionally.

questions.question: Why is spring an especially strong page to study?
questions.answer: Because it displays life returning in many forms all at once.

questions.question: What is significant about the phrase that forms emerge from simple material?
questions.answer: It points to the difference between plain substance and the highly ordered living shapes that come from it.

questions.question: What does the spreading of seeds teach about life on earth?
questions.answer: It teaches that continuation of life is arranged through purposeful methods.

questions.question: How are feeding and raising living things described?
questions.answer: They are described as careful, efficient, and full of mercy.

questions.question: Why does the passage stress the variety of foods?
questions.answer: To show the richness of provision given to creatures with different needs.

questions.question: What is the effect of saying these provisions come from an unseen treasury?
questions.answer: It directs the mind to a source of generosity beyond visible material causes.

questions.question: How does the example of babies and mothers make the argument more personal?
questions.answer: It brings the sign of mercy into everyday human experience where need and care are very clear.

questions.question: What conclusion should a thoughtful person draw from that example?
questions.answer: That such fitting and tender provision points to a Merciful Creator.

questions.question: How is the earth after winter like the dead being raised?
questions.answer: What seemed lifeless becomes active and living again, showing a pattern of renewal.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect spring with Allah’s power over all things?
questions.answer: Because reviving the earth on such a vast scale shows ability without limit.

questions.question: Summarize the traveler’s final understanding from this section.
questions.answer: He sees the earth as a many-layered witness that declares Allah’s mercy, power, and oneness.

questions.question: What question from the earth redirects the traveler’s search?
questions.answer: The earth asks why he is roaming through the upper world and invites him to look closer at the earth instead.

questions.question: What does the image of a turning dervish add to the description of the globe?
questions.answer: It gives a sense of lively, graceful motion while still pointing to a meaningful pattern.

questions.question: Which time cycles are tied to the earth’s movement here?
questions.answer: The passage ties its movement to the sequence of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the earth’s journey through space important to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that even while moving through vast space, it remains steady and fit for carrying life.

questions.question: What does the traveler discover when reading the earth’s “chapters”?
questions.answer: He discovers many signs that testify to the One who governs and sustains the earth.

questions.question: What particular subject on the earth’s page does he examine?
questions.answer: He examines how living beings are created, spread, and cared for in spring.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast simplicity and complexity?
questions.answer: It shows highly detailed living forms coming from plain and simple materials.

questions.question: What role do flying seeds play in the spring scene?
questions.answer: They are a sign of the organized spreading of life to many places.

questions.question: How is the feeding of creatures described in emotional as well as practical terms?
questions.answer: It is shown as both efficient and deeply compassionate.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by describing spring provision as being sent from a hidden storehouse?
questions.answer: It suggests that the true giver of provision is a merciful Lord whose resources are beyond what we see.

questions.question: Why is milk for infants one of the strongest examples in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows perfectly matched care for a vulnerable creature at the exact moment of need.

questions.question: What does this example teach about Allah’s attributes?
questions.answer: It points to mercy, generosity, wisdom, and loving care.

questions.question: How does the Qur’anic verse about bringing the earth to life relate to resurrection?
questions.answer: It teaches that the One who revives the land can also bring dead people back to life.

questions.question: Why is spring called a demonstration rather than just a season?
questions.answer: Because it actively displays truths about mercy, power, and resurrection in a visible way.

questions.question: What statement of faith is echoed by all the earth’s pages in this passage?
questions.answer: They all point to the truth that no one deserves worship except Allah.
